subject: Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?

messages.author: 9e6d73d28cc25e70
messages.subject: Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?
parts:
Could I just encode each SNP in my genotype file to (A,H,B) to
represent major homo, heterozygous, and minor homo?

I tried "ehk" and "imp" methods in R/qtl, and it looks fine, but I am
not sure it is an appropriate way or not, and whether the methods
specifically take the cross structure information into the analysis,
When I load that file by read.cross, it reports the data type is "F2"
cross.

Thanks!

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?
parts:
It would be best to omit the hetererozygous genotypes and convert the cross type to "risib" or "riself" (according to whether the RIL are by sibling mating or selfing. There are functions convert2risib and convert2riself to facilitate this.

karl

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Is it appropriate to use scanone function directly on a genotype file from a RIL population ?
parts: > I think that will make r/qtl lose power to detect QTL. Is that right?
Not necessarily, but I'm assuming that your RIL lines are close to inbred and so there should be only a very small proportion of heterozygous genotypes.

> Actually, I want to find a general implementation of Haley-Knott
> regression and Imputation based regression from Sen and Churchill, are
> these two implementation in R/qtl are specifically designed for cross
> data?
